entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Psamtik II, known by the Graeco-Romans as Psammetichus or Psammeticus, was a king of the Saite-based Twenty-sixth Dynasty of Egypt.

Born to Necho II, he ascended to the throne around 610 BCE and reigned until his death in 588 BCE. During his reign, Psamtik II implemented significant administrative reforms, re-established trade with the Phoenicians, and expanded Egypt's borders through military campaigns.

One of Psamtik II's most notable achievements was the construction of a new capital city, Naucratis, which served as a major center for trade and commerce. His reign also saw a resurgence of Egyptian culture, as he promoted the worship of ancient Egyptian gods and encouraged the development of new artistic and literary works.

Psamtik II's legacy extended beyond his own time, as he played a crucial role in shaping the course of Egyptian history and influencing the development of the Hellenistic period. His reign marked the beginning of a new era in Egyptian history, one that would be shaped by the interplay between Egyptian and Greek cultures.

The iconic inscription on the statue of Psamtik II, which boasts the phrase 'I am a god', underscores the king's ambitions to elevate Egypt to a divine status, and his vision for a unified and powerful Egypt that would transcend its geographical boundaries.
